frequency_question: How often do central bank principals execute temporary liquidity impounding tools when system liquidity surpasses predetermined threshold targets within their operational window?
membership_rule: Includes instances of incremental or ad-hoc cash reserve ratios or equivalent targeted secondary liquidity impounding mandates deployed by major central banks; excludes routine primary reserve ratio adjustments made during scheduled bi-monthly monetary policy reviews unless specifically formatted as an incremental add-on tool.

cases.name: PBOC targeted reserve requirement ratio adjustments for excess liquidity
Bank Indonesia secondary reserve requirement modifications
Central Bank of Nigeria cash reserve requirement debits for liquidity management

provenance_note: 4 cases named, 6 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.5x)
coverage_note: 4 named historical instances of targeted secondary reserve ratio tools deployed during liquidity surges; estimated roughly 6 total historical occurrences across major emerging markets.
known_gaps: Excludes minor or opaque administrative liquidity absorption operations that did not use formal incremental reserve terminology.
skeleton: Central banks facing severe post-crisis or surge-driven excess liquidity conditions deploy secondary reserve ratio add-ons roughly once every major liquidity surge cycle.
multiplier: 4 observed deployable actions across 6 major emerging market jurisdictions over 24 years experiencing structural liquidity overhangs.
validity_reason: Central banking liquidity management frameworks and statutory authorities for reserve ratio adjustments remain stable across medium-term economic cycles.
